narrative:
The model predicted a 65% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold used by the admissions process, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. By far the strongest influence was your third-year class ranking. Placing in the second decile is noticeably lower than the average of accepted students (around the sixth decile). This single piece of information pushed the prediction strongly toward failure.

Your LSAT score of 38 worked in the opposite direction. It sits slightly above the average of accepted applicants and therefore pulled the prediction modestly toward passing. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.40 also helped a bit; it is higher than the typical GPA among those who were admitted. Unfortunately, these positive signals were not large enough to overcome the substantial negative impact of your third-year performance.

You should focus on strengthening your academic record in any remaining coursework, consider retaking the LSAT if you can improve it meaningfully, and explore schools or programs that weigh later-year improvement more heavily. Building a stronger upward trend before reapplying will give the model a very different picture of your likelihood of success. (218 words)
